lesson.title: Containers from Zero, part 9: when something fails
lesson.description: Add health checks and restart policies to the notes app, then break it three ways on purpose: stop the database, drop a setting, end the database process. Match each failure to the state, the logs and what Docker did.
lesson.tested: Caused and read all three failures with Compose v5.8.0 and Engine 29.10.1, 25 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: A health check reports; a restart policy reacts to an exit. Neither fixes a wrong setting, and the logs say which one you have.

cheatsheet.intro: Health checks, restart policies and how to read a failure, from Lesson 9.

boards.title: Health check

rows.name: test
rows.role: Command run inside the container; exit 0 is healthy, 1 is unhealthy.

rows.name: interval, timeout
rows.role: How often the check runs, and how long one run may take.

rows.name: retries
rows.role: Failures in a row before the status is `unhealthy`.

rows.name: start_period
rows.role: Start-up time when failures do not count.

boards.note: Status: `starting`, `healthy`, `unhealthy`. Read by `depends_on: condition: service_healthy` and `up --wait`. It never restarts anything.

boards.title: Restart policy

rows.name: on-failure:5
rows.role: The process exits with a non-zero code, at most 5 times.

rows.name: unless-stopped
rows.role: The process exits, with any code.
rows.where: you stopped it, e.g. `docker compose stop`

rows.name: always
rows.role: The container stops, until it is removed.
rows.where: you stopped it; it returns when the daemon or the container is restarted

boards.note: A manual stop is not undone by the policy. An unhealthy container that keeps running is not restarted.

steps.title: What the lab showed
steps.hint: IDs and times differ on your machine

items.what: `db` Waiting, Healthy; then `web` Started and Healthy; the first `curl` listed the notes.
`database unavailable`; web log: `failed to resolve host 'db'`. After 35 s, web `Up (unhealthy)`, `restarts=0`.
`exited exit=1 restarts=5`; six lines of `DATABASE_URL is not set`; it stayed `Exited (1)`.
`received smart shutdown request`, then `running exit=0 restarts=1` and healthy again.

steps.note: Safety: publishes 127.0.0.1:8080 and stops services on purpose; no data is deleted. Undo with `docker compose up -d --wait` and delete `compose.broken.yaml`.

homework.intro: Use the notes folder from the lesson. IDs and times will differ. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: What are the three health statuses, and what makes a container `unhealthy`?
exercises.a: `starting`, `healthy`, `unhealthy`. It becomes `unhealthy` after `retries` failed checks in a row.

exercises.q: When does Docker apply a restart policy?
exercises.a: When the container's main process exits. It does not look at the health status.

exercises.q: What is the difference between `on-failure:5` and `unless-stopped`?
exercises.a: `on-failure:5` restarts after a non-zero exit, at most five times. `unless-stopped` restarts after any exit, unless you stopped the container.

exercises.q: Why does web's check use Python instead of `curl`?
exercises.a: `python:3.14-slim` has neither `curl` nor `wget`, and the check runs inside the container.

exercises.q: What does `condition: service_healthy` change at start-up?
exercises.a: Compose waits for `db` to be healthy before it starts `web`.

exercises.q: Run `docker compose up -d --wait`, then `curl /notes.txt`. Why does the first request work now?
exercises.a: `--wait` returned only after both services were healthy, and web's check needs a working database.

exercises.q: Run `docker compose stop db`, wait 35 seconds, and inspect web. What is its status and restart count?
exercises.a: `Up (unhealthy)`, `restarts=0`. Its process never exited, so no restart policy applied.

exercises.q: What does web's log say while `db` is stopped?
exercises.a: `failed to resolve host 'db'`: a stopped container leaves the network.

exercises.q: Start web with `compose.broken.yaml`. What do `docker inspect` and `docker compose logs web` show?
exercises.a: `exited exit=1 restarts=5` and six lines of `DATABASE_URL is not set`: one start and five restarts.

exercises.q: Run `docker compose exec db kill 1`. What happens to `db`?
exercises.a: PostgreSQL logs `received smart shutdown request` and exits with 0; `unless-stopped` starts it again, `restarts=1`.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: db's check always fails. What does `docker compose up -d` print?
exercises.a: `dependency failed to start: container notes-db-1 is unhealthy`, and web is not started.

exercises.q: You change web's policy to `on-failure` with no number and start it with the empty setting. What happens?
exercises.a: Docker keeps restarting it, because no retry limit is set. The log grows by one line per start.

exercises.q: `db` had `on-failure:5` instead of `unless-stopped`. What does `kill 1` do?
exercises.a: PostgreSQL exits with 0, which is not a failure, so it stays stopped.

exercises.q: A web check uses `curl` on `python:3.14-slim`. What does the health log say?
exercises.a: `exec: "curl": executable file not found in $PATH`, and the check fails.
